text:
arai-people: Quick policy question  Marta's team has a contractor (temp) who signed an offer to convert to full-time on 2027-01-10. Manager asked whether we can: (1) retroactively credit PTO accrual for the months they were on payroll as a temp (they were paid on payroll, not 1099), and (2) allow carryover of up to 2 unused PTO days across year-end into the new FT period. Note: their contract year ends 2026-12-31 and blackout is Dec 20Dec 31. Marta, can you summarize the ask?

marta-manager: Manager here. They joined 2026-06-15 as a fixed-term on payroll at 0.9 FTE. We offered conversion to FT with start 2027-01-10. They have 1.5 days PTO left at year-end. Team coverage around holidays is tight so wed like to either (A) carry 2 days forward into their FT balance, or (B) convert 2 days into a one-time payroll credit if carryovers are blocked by accounting. Which is easier?

diego-payroll: FYI payroll rules: if the worker was on payroll (W2) then they accrued per FTE already unless the original contract explicitly excluded accrual. Retroactive accrual adjustments are allowed but require People Ops + Finance approval because of accounting. Fastest operational path = one-time accrual adjustment entry or a payout. Examples we accept: 

```
worker_id, action, days, note
90521, ACCRUAL_ADJ, 2, "retro accrual for conversion to FT; manager confirm on thread"
```

OR for payout: 

```
90521, PTO_PAYOUT, 2, "one-time payout for unused PTO due to conversion accounting"
```

Send to payroll@redwood.com and cc people-ops + finance. If you want balancing on books (carryover into FT), Finance must accept the accrual adjustment before fiscal close.

yvonne-legal: Legal note: ensure the offer letter/FT agreement documents the conversion date and any retroactive PTO treatment. If you promise carryover in the offer, add an amendment and attach to the HR file. Also avoid language that implies guaranteed future accrual beyond the amendment.

arai-people: Additional People Ops guidance: Policy baseline = employees on payroll normally accrue per policy; however fixed-term hires sometimes have "no accrual" language in the contract. Check the original contract. If the contract already granted accrual, carryover rules for employees apply. If not, we can still do a one-time exception but must document an addendum and route to Finance. Given year-end blackout (2026-12-20 to 2026-12-31) any exception that impacts payroll must be submitted early.

marta-manager: Contract says "limited benefits; PTO not included". So they technically didn't accrue. We still want to offer a 2-day goodwill credit when they convert to FT.

diego-payroll: Because the contract excluded PTO, we can't retroactively create accruals without exception. Two choices operationally: (1) Add a 2-day accrual adjustment effective 2027-01-10 (ACCRUAL_ADJ) so it shows up on FT balance (requires Finance ok), or (2) payroll one-time credit (PTO_ACCT_ADJ) or cash payout. Example CSV for accrual on conversion date: 

```
worker_id, action, days, effective_date, note
90521, ACCRUAL_ADJ, 2, 2027-01-10, "conversion goodwill credit per manager email"
```

If Finance declines accrual we can do a payout: 

```
90521, PTO_PAYOUT, 2, "conversion goodwill payout"
```

Send to payroll@redwood.com and cc people-ops + finance + legal.

yvonne-legal: If you choose accrual on conversion, add the amendment to the new FT offer packet: "Upon conversion on 2027-01-10 employee will receive a one-time credit of 2 PTO days." Manager signature + employee signature required. Also note blackout constraints for scheduling immediate time off during 2026-12-20 to 2026-12-31.

calendar-bot: Reminder: Year-end blackout 2026-12-20 to 2026-12-31. Any time-off during blackout requires Manager + People Ops approval in writing.

marta-manager: Ok plan: we'll (A) add the amendment to the FT offer that grants 2 PTO days effective 2027-01-10; (B) if Finance approves, payroll will run the ACCRUAL_ADJ with effective date 2027-01-10; (C) if Finance denies, we'll do PTO_PAYOUT before fiscal close. I'll confirm here once amendment signed. Which is the fastest to get employee access to days in Jan if they want to book travel?

diego-payroll: Fastest to guarantee money = PTO_PAYOUT processed before fiscal close (deadline 2026-12-18). Fastest to guarantee days in HRIS = ACCRUAL_ADJ effective 2027-01-10 but requires Finance sign-off and amendment signed before start of conversion. If the employee wants to book travel for early Jan, you can provisionally approve unpaid time-off or request a comp-day from the team for coverage; doc everything in thread.

arai-people: I'll prep the amendment template and start Finance pre-approval request. Marta please attach the signed amendment to the People Ops ticket. If payroll needs interim coverage, consider a comp-day or manager-approved unpaid day.

marta-manager: Will do. Employee is okay waiting for Jan 10 accrual but asked for a note so they can tentatively plan travel. I'll add a DM confirmation now and post the signed amendment here when done. Thanks team :thumbsup:
